**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Yes — extensively. Melchizedek as "king of righteousness" (Heb 7:2, VSG M26-A1-007) is a typological figure. Wisdom who "walks in the paths of righteousness" (Pro 8:20, VSG M26-A1-007) participates typologically in Messianic-divine quality. The righteous Branch (Jer 23:6; 33:16), the righteous Servant (Isa 53:11), the Messianic king who is "righteous and having salvation" (Zec 9:9) — all are typological deployments pointing toward Christ as the incarnate expression of divine righteousness.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — Noah's righteousness (Heb 11:7, VSG 4846-001) is typological: his righteous act of building the ark in faith points toward the righteousness that comes by faith in Christ. Abraham's credited righteousness (Rom 4:3–9, VSG 3410-001) is explicitly typological in Paul's argument: Abraham's case is a type of the faith-righteousness available to all believers.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** The Messianic scepter of uprightness (Heb 1:8, VSG 1218-001) is explicitly typological — the uprightness of the Messianic king's rule is the perfected instantiation of what the uprightness vocabulary names.

**[C — Justification]** Yes — the entire OT judicial vocabulary (tsa.deq, 947-002: acquitting the innocent) is typological in relation to divine justification. The human courtroom (Deu 25:1) is a type of the divine courtroom; the acquittal of the innocent is a type of the justification of the ungodly by faith.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — Moses' act of avenging the oppressed Israelite (Act 7:24, VSG 945-001) is identified as part of the pattern of Israel's rejection of its deliverer, pointing toward Christ. The persistent widow's cry (Luk 18:3–8, VSG 944-001) is deployed by Jesus as a type of the elect's eschatological cry for divine justice.

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — the Ninevites' repentance as a condemnation of unrepentant Israel (Mat 12:41–42; Luk 11:31–32, VSG 4846-001) is typological: a past generation's response to less light condemns a present generation's response to greater light.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Abraham's faith being counted as righteousness (Rom 4:3–9, VSG 3410-001) is the most extensively worked typological passage in the cluster. Paul explicitly uses Abraham's case as a type applicable to all who believe.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** The structural opposites do not appear to be deployed typologically in the verse evidence. They define the boundary of righteousness but are not used to point toward a greater reality. Silence noted.

**[CLUSTER]** Typological use of righteousness-vocabulary is extensive and structurally important across the cluster — A1, A2, B, C, D, E, and F all show typological deployment. The pattern is consistently Christological: OT instances of righteousness point toward Christ as the one who fulfils, exceeds, and incarnates the divine righteousness that was only partially visible in the OT types. G is the sole silence.

findings.finding_value: M01-A has clear typological use. **[CHAR-1]** E — The corpus contains clear typological deployment of wilful sinning in two directions. First, Eze 28:16 ("you sinned; so I cast you as a profane thing from the mountain of God, O guardian cherub") uses the cherub's sinning as a paradigmatic instance that illuminates the inner dynamic of how sinning produces expulsion from the divine presence — a pattern that maps onto human sinning and its consequences. Second, the Levitical sin-offering system (VCG-04: Lev 4:14, 4:22, 4:23, 4:27, 4:28, 4:35, 5:6–13) is typological throughout — the sacrificial remedy for wilful sinning points forward to the substitutionary atonement that resolves sin's debt. The Lev 5:13 formula ("and he shall be forgiven") and Lev 4:35 ("the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin which he has committed, and he shall be forgiven") foreshadow a forgiving transaction that the NT corpus (VCG-05) casts as fulfilled in Christ's advocacy (1Jo 2:1: "we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous").

**[CHAR-10]** E — Limited typological evidence. Act 21:21's apostasy charge against Paul operates in the context of the Acts narrative's broader argument about the relationship between the Mosaic covenant and the new covenant: the accusation that Paul teaches apostasy from Moses is itself addressed within the narrative's argument that Paul is not abandoning the covenant but fulfilling it through Christ. This is not typology in the strict sense but covenantal-hermeneutical deployment: the apostasia charge is the occasion for clarifying what authentic covenantal identity means in the new-covenant era.

**[CHAR-11]** E — Yes — in two directions. (1) *Adam as type*: Rom 5:12/14 — "just as sin came into the world through one man... Adam, who was a type of the one who was to come" — Adam's original sin-entry is the negative type that establishes the universal condition; Christ as the antitype reverses what Adam established. The typological use of sin's universal entry (through one man) points toward sin's universal removal (through one man — the last Adam). (2) *Israel's trespass as type*: Rom 11:11/12 — "through their trespass salvation has come to the Gentiles" — Israel's corporate participation in the universal sinful condition becomes the occasion for the redemptive purpose to extend to all nations; the trespass is deployed typologically as the instrument of unexpected global blessing.

**[CHAR-12]** E — Yes. Gal 3:22 — "the Scripture imprisoned everything under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe" — the universal imprisonment under sin functions typologically: the condition of universal imprisonment is the necessary precondition and backdrop against which the promise by faith operates. The imprisonment-type is not an end in itself but points toward the faith-promise as its resolution. The negative type (imprisonment under sin) points toward the positive antitype (liberation through faith in Jesus Christ). The typological use is explicitly purposive: "so that the promise... might be given."

**[CHAR-13]** E — Yes. (1) *Day of Atonement typology*: Lev 16:21 — "Aaron shall lay both his hands on the head of the live goat, and confess over it all the iniquities of the people of Israel, and all their transgressions, all their sins. And he shall put them on the head of the goat and send it away into the wilderness" — the annual ritual of sin-record being placed on the scapegoat and sent to the wilderness typologically points toward the Lamb of God (Joh 1:29 — "who takes away the sin of the world"). (2) *Moses's divine-book intercession*: Exo 32:32 — Moses's offer to be blotted from God's book if the people's sin is not forgiven typologically prefigures Christ's bearing the sin-record of the people.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Yes — the most concentrated typological evidence in M10. The entire VCG-01 kip.pu.rim system (12 verses) is typological: the Day of Atonement (Lev 23:27/28; 25:9), the daily sin offerings (Exo 29:36; 30:10), and the priestly bearing of iniquity (Lev 10:17) all function as institutional types pointing toward the antitypical atoning work of Christ. Mat 26:28 — "my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins" — is the antitype declaration: the covenant blood replaces the animal blood; the permanent forgiveness replaces the annual provisional covering.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Yes — through Isa 43:27's structure. "Your first father sinned, and your mediators transgressed against me" — the naming of the "first father" as the origin-point of Israel's sinning functions as the typological ground: the ancestral sinning is the type that the present generation's condition fulfils. The first father's sin becomes the pattern that the mediators continued and the present nation inherits — a typological escalation-chain where the ancestral type is expanded and confirmed in each subsequent generation.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Yes. Rom 5:19 — "by the one man's disobedience the many were made sinners, so by the one man's obedience the many will be made righteous" — the sinner-identity constituted through Adam is the type that Christ's righteousness reverses; Adam as the type of the sinner-constituting one, Christ as the antitype of the righteous-constituting one. 1Ti 1:15/16 — Paul as the "foremost sinner" functions paradigmatically: the mercy shown to him (the worst case) becomes a demonstration for all future believers that Christ's saving mission extends to the extreme sinner-type.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Yes — through the transference dimension (VCG-03). Exo 28:38 — "Aaron shall bear any guilt from the holy things that the people of Israel consecrate" — the high priest's guilt-bearing on his forehead is typological: Aaron as the one who bears the community's guilt before God prefigures the NT sin-bearer. Eze 4:4/5/6 — the prophet Ezekiel is commanded to bear Israel's and Judah's punishment symbolically by lying on his side — the enacted guilt-bearing is typological of the servant-bearing of iniquity (Isa 53:12 — "he bore the sin of many" — in CHAR-13's corpus).

**[CHAR-18]** E — Yes — through the servant-bearing passages (VCG-06 Isa 53 sub-set). Isa 53:5 — "he was crushed for our iniquities" — the servant's bearing of the people's accumulated iniquity is typological: the priestly scapegoat bearing (Lev 16:21/22 — VCG-01) is the OT type; the servant's bearing is the eschatological fulfilment-type pointing toward Christ. Isa 53:6 — "the Lord has laid on him the iniquity of us all" — the universal scope of the iniquity-bearing is the typological pinnacle: all accumulated human iniquity placed upon the one servant. Zec 3:4 — "I have taken your iniquity away from you" — Joshua's single-person iniquity-removal prefigures the land's total removal (Zec 3:9) and the new covenant's complete forgiveness (Jer 31:34).

**[CHAR-19]** E — Yes — through two typological axes. (1) *Adam-paradigm transgression* (VCG-05): Rom 5:14 — "Adam... a type of the one who was to come" — Adam's transgression is explicitly named as a type; the trespass's death-consequence (VCG-05 — Rom 5:15/16/17) is the negative type whose positive antitype is Christ's one act of righteousness; (2) *Servant-bearing* (VCG-07 cross-reference; VCG-06): Isa 53:5 — "he was pierced for our transgressions"; Isa 53:8 — "stricken for the transgression of my people" — the servant's bearing of transgression's cost is the OT type pointing toward Christ. Isa 53:12 — "numbered with the transgressors; yet he bore the sin of many, and makes intercession for the transgressors" — the intercession-for-transgressors is the typological bridge.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The cultic-purification corpus (VCG-02) carries clear typological freight. The daily sin offering for the altar (Exo 29:36 — "every day you shall offer a bull as a sin offering for atonement... you shall purify the altar... and anoint it to consecrate it") is part of a larger typological system: the repeated daily and annual cleansing of the altar and sanctuary (Eze 45:18) points toward a final, comprehensive atonement that the sacrificial system cannot itself achieve but only anticipates. The individual unintentional-sin offering (Num 15:27/28 — goat offered, priest makes atonement, forgiven) similarly functions typologically: the external remedy for an inadvertent moral failure anticipates a remedy that addresses the inner moral condition more completely than a prescribed animal sacrifice can. Lev 4:3 (priestly sin implicating the community) prefigures the priest-as-representative who mediates between the community and God.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Yes — through two typological axes. (1) *The marital-faithlessness type of Israel's unfaithfulness to God*: Jer 3:20 — "as a treacherous wife leaves her husband, so have you been treacherous to me, O house of Israel" — the marital faithlessness is the type of the Israel-God covenant betrayal; Mal 2:14-16 — marital faithlessness is treated with the same theological seriousness as covenant-faithlessness toward God; the marriage-covenant is the human type pointing toward the divine-Israel bond; (2) *Adam-type covenant-breaking*: Hos 6:7 — "like Adam they transgressed the covenant; there they dealt faithlessly with me" — Adam's covenant-breach is the founding type of which Israel's faithlessness is the national repetition.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Yes — through the vine-degeneracy type and the creature-creator inversion type. (1) *Vine type*: Jer 2:21 — "I planted you a choice vine... how then have you turned degenerate and become a wild vine?" — Israel's degeneracy is the anti-type of the faithfully-producing vine; this vine-type points toward the true vine (Joh 15 — in CHAR-20's adjacent cluster); (2) *Creature-creator inversion*: Isa 29:16 — "shall the potter be regarded as the clay... 'He did not make me'?" — the cognitive inversion of creature denying creator is the type of the ultimate eschatological reversal in which God will act as the definitive potter who reshapes the perverted creation.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Yes — through the Christological substitution type. 1Pe 3:18 — "Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring us to God" — the unjust (*adikoi*) are the precise moral category for whom the righteous Christ substitutes; the unrighteous/unjust person-type is the direct object of Christ's redemptive action. The unjust person-type (VCG-03 — *adikos*) is deployed typologically: the human category of the unjust points toward the divine provision of the righteous One who takes their place.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes, in two directions. (1) *The corporate confessional sequence as typological pattern*: the Judges-Samuel pattern (Judg 10:10/15; 1Sa 7:6; 12:10) — confession leading to divine intervention and leadership renewal — is a recurring pattern that typologically prefigures the deeper restoration in which the new covenant provides a once-for-all resolution of what corporate confession could only address episodically. (2) *Daniel's prayer (Dan 9:5/8/11/15)* functions typologically: a righteous man praying on behalf of a sinful community, including himself in the confession, points forward to the intercessory representative who identifies with the sinners he confesses for. The sustained, comprehensive character of Daniel's confession — multiple specific dimensions named — anticipates the total coverage of sin that the new covenant promises.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The 8-verse corpus contains no typological deployment of conscience suppression. The verses address the characteristic directly as a present moral condition (Jer 2:35; Jer 16:10) or as a described inner state (Ecc 8:12; Tit 3:11; 1Cor 15:34). No verse deploys it to point toward a christological, eschatological, or covenantal reality beyond the immediate. Judg 20:16 is physically literal with no inner-being content.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Limited typological deployment. The Kings Jeroboam-pattern corpus (1Ki 16:31; 2Ki 3:3; 10:29/31; 13:2/6/11; 14:24; 15:9/18/24/28) functions as a *cumulative typological warning*: each king who "did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam" both perpetuates the sin and adds to the typological portrait of a leadership class whose refusal to turn models — and transmits — a pattern of sustained refusal. This cumulative pattern typologically anticipates the NT's sharpest formulation in Heb 10:26: the persistent, deliberate sinning after knowing the truth as the ultimate form of refusal to repent. The OT pattern points toward the NT's eschatological intensification.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes. Heb 3:17 deploys the wilderness generation's 40 years of habitual sinning typologically: "Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?" — the wilderness generation's sustained habitual rebellion is presented as a *warning type* for the Hebrews 3 audience. The OT instance of 40-year habitual sinning functions as the negative typological precedent: this is what happens when the inner pattern of rebellion is sustained — the bodies fall. The typology warns the NT community against repeating the pattern. The direction is human instance (wilderness generation) → warning application to human readers.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Yes. The Jeroboam-formula ("who made Israel to sin") operates as a *negative typological benchmark* — Jeroboam is the established type of the sin-transmitting leader against whom every subsequent king is measured. 2Ki 23:15 — Josiah's destruction of Jeroboam's altar — is typologically significant: the dismantling of the physical monument to Jeroboam's contagious sin points toward the eschatological dismantling of all sin-transmitting structures. The altar at Bethel was the enduring structural legacy of Jeroboam's contagious sin; its demolition under Josiah prefigures the complete removal of the structures that sin-transmitting leadership builds. The OT pattern thus points forward to a leadership that transmits righteousness rather than sin — the antitype of Jeroboam is the leader through whom God's people are formed toward God rather than away from him.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Limited typological evidence. 1Ki 12:19 / 2Ch 10:19 — "Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day" — the narrator's summary functions as a theological-historical marker that points forward: Israel's persistent political revolt from the Davidic house is an ongoing wound in the covenant history that ultimately points toward the eschatological restoration of the Davidic covenant (the hope of the restored Davidic king). The political revolt marks a fracture in the covenant history that requires future divine resolution. The typological direction is: the present fracture anticipating future restoration.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Yes. VCG-02's blasphemy-charge against Jesus (Mat 26:65; Mar 14:64; Luk 5:21; Joh 10:33) operates typologically: the religious authorities' charge of blasphemy against Jesus — based on his claim to divine authority and his forgiveness of sins — is the type that ironically inverts; the one accused of blasphemy is actually the one who is God. The typological direction is: the human accusation of blasphemy (false, directed against the true Son of God) points toward the revelation of who Jesus is — the charge that is meant to condemn becomes the evidence that he is what he claims.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence contains limited but present typological use. The most analytically significant instance is Dan 12:10's eschatological frame (M10b-A-VCG-05): "the wicked shall act wickedly and none of the wicked shall understand" — here the wicked person is a type of those who will harden in the final purification rather than being refined. Isa 53:9 (M10b-A-VCG-04) is typologically important in the opposite direction: the servant is buried "among the wicked" despite having no wickedness in him — the wicked person's category functions typologically here as a contrast-type that reveals the servant's inner purity by negation. The Ezekiel repentance-corpus (VCG-07) does not function typologically in the strict sense but does prefigure the prophetic call to inner turning that the NT develops. The wicked-as-type is primarily eschatological (those destined for judgment) and contrast-typological (the negative against which the righteous, the servant, and the Messiah are defined).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The evidence contains limited but present typological use. Mat 12:45 (vc=65879 — VCG-06) is the most concentrated typological instance: spirits more evil filling a vacated inner space, and the generation mirroring this increasing inner wickedness — the individual's inner dynamics are typological of the generation's collective condition. Mat 13:49 (vc=14459 — VCG-04) deploys the evil/righteous distinction eschatologically — the separation at the end of the age functions as a typological culmination of the present moral category. Gal 1:4 (vc=14466 — VCG-01) names "the present evil age" as what Christ's self-giving rescues from — here the cosmic frame of evil is typological, pointing beyond the present age to the coming age of liberation. The typological use is primarily eschatological.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The evidence contains significant typological use. Rev 17:4-5 (vc=23, 65878 — VCG-02/05) is the most concentrated typological deployment: Babylon the Great as the "mother of prostitutes and of earth's abominations" — the abomination category is deployed at a cosmic typological scale where historical Babylon/Rome becomes the type of all earthly systems constituted by abomination. Rev 21:27 (vc=22 — VCG-05): the eschatological city's exclusion of the abominable is a typological culmination, pointing from the OT's ritual exclusion of the defiled beyond the sacred boundary toward the final eschatological separation. Eze 9:4 (vc=1698 — VCG-04): the mark on those who grieve over abominations prefigures the Lamb's book of life distinction (Rev 21:27). The typological direction is primarily from OT moral-character abomination categories toward NT/Revelation eschatological and cosmic deployment.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. VCG-06 (5V — Dan 9:27; 11:31; 12:11; Mat 24:15; Mar 13:14) is the typological corpus: the "abomination of desolation" is the most explicit typological use, where present idolatrous abomination patterns (sanctuary desecration) point toward an eschatological peak-evil event. Mat 24:15 (vc=65876 — VCG-06): "when you see the abomination of desolation spoken of by the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place" — the historical desecration of Daniel's prophecy is typologically extended to future sacrilege. Hos 9:10 (vc=1632 — VCG-04): consecration to Baal-peor and becoming detestable like the idol is typological of the idolatry pattern throughout Israel's history. The Ezekiel VCG-05 corpus is typologically significant as the concentrated portrait of how accumulated abominations drive the divine presence away — a pattern the NT echoes in its understanding of defilement and divine departure.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The evidence shows typological use primarily in the prophetic projection of iniquity as scheming toward its own judgment endpoint. Isa 10:1 (vc=38191 — VCG-02): "Woe to those who decree iniquitous decrees" — the institutionalised scheming of the oppressive ruler is deployed as a prophetic type of the kind of inner evil that draws divine woe. The Psalms' evildoer corpus (VCG-03) establishes the evildoer as a type — a recurring figure whose inner scheming and ultimate defeat function typologically across the Psalter to express the certainty of divine justice. Psa 92:7-9 (vc=38246/38247 — VCG-03): "evildoers flourish… doomed to destruction forever… enemies shall perish; all evildoers shall be scattered" — this pattern functions as a typological teaching about the trajectory of all iniquity. The typological use is primarily didactic-judicial: iniquity as scheming functions as the type of what incurs divine judgment.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes. The Revelation VCG-01 corpus is the most concentrated typological use: Rev 13:6 (vc=14356 — VCG-01): the beast's sustained blasphemy against God's name and dwelling is a typological figure — the beast-figure represents the concentrated eschatological expression of all blasphemous defiance. The three Rev 16 verses (vc=14352; 14350; 14353 — VCG-01) show the human population under judgment as instances of the same blasphemous-will pattern at eschatological scale. Jude 8-10 (vc=14354; 14355 — VCG-01) deploys the dreamers as a typological figure linking to Sodom and past instances of rebellion. The VCG-03 false-accusation corpus (Joh 18:30 — vc=14378) has clear christological typological significance: the false charge against the accused as an evildoer participating in the pattern of false accusation against the righteous that culminates in the trial of Jesus.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six characteristics evidence typological use, and the cluster-scope pattern is a consistent eschatological-direction typology with one christological supplement. All six deploy their inner-evil forms as types pointing toward eschatological judgment — the present human instances of wickedness, evil, abomination, iniquity, and evil speech function as types of the eschatological culmination of those patterns. The pattern is most concentrated in Chars 3 and 4 (the abomination-of-desolation typological progression: OT individual acts of abomination → eschatological peak-sacrilege event) and Char 6 (Rev 13:6 — the beast's blasphemy as the eschatological type of all human blasphemous defiance). Char 1 contributes a contrast-typological instance (Isa 53:9 — the servant among the wicked, revealing purity by contrast with wickedness). Char 6 contributes the cluster's primary christological typological instance (Joh 18:30 — the false charge against Jesus as evildoer, the pattern of false accusation against the innocent culminating in the trial of the righteous one). The cluster's typological use is thus: eschatological-judgment pointing (all six) + christological contrast-and-revelation pointing (Chars 1 and 6 specifically).

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, at two points in the characteristic's 133-verse corpus. First, Num 19 (M10c-A-VCG-07): the red-heifer purification rite — the most elaborate response to the most severe defilement (corpse-contact) — is treated in the NT as a type of the blood of Christ (cited in Heb 9:13-14, though that verse is not in the M10c corpus). Within the corpus itself, the rite's structure — a sin offering preserved as a standing remedy for the entire congregation, administered through water — anticipates a purification economy beyond its own scope (Num 19:9: "it is a sin offering"). Second, the NT akathartos categorical revision (M10c-B-VCG-05: Act 10:14/28): the defilement category that shaped Peter's conscience is used by the divine vision to signal the covenantal transition — "what God has made clean, do not call unclean" (Act 10:28). The ritual-defilement-state category is deployed typologically as the boundary whose revision marks the new-covenant's extension to the nations.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes, in two moves evidenced in the corpus. First, the Hebrew prophetic register provides typological scaffolding for the NT moral-inner register: Job 14:4 (VCG-01), Isa 6:5 (VCG-01), and Isa 64:6 (VCG-01) all express the constitutional moral-inner defilement of the human before God, which the NT then addresses directly in terms of the gospel and sanctification. The Hebrew voices point forward to a problem the NT claims is addressed in Christ. Second, the positive-inverse in Rev 14:4 (VCG-05) — "these have not defiled themselves... they follow the Lamb... redeemed from mankind as firstfruits" — is explicitly christological-eschatological: the undefiled inner condition is defined in relation to the Lamb, constituting a typological participation in the Lamb's purity. The few in Rev 3:4 (VCG-05) who have "not soiled their garments" will "walk with me in white" — the white garments are eschatological, pointing toward divine fullness.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes, in two directions. First, the land-defilement register (VCG-04) and sanctuary-defilement register (VCG-03) function typologically in the prophetic corpus: the desecration of the physical land and temple in the pre-exilic prophets points forward to the eschatological restoration (Eze 37:23, Isa 52:1, Zec 13:1, VCG-05) in which both are permanently cleansed. The physical defilement and restoration is the type; the eschatological fullness is the antitype. Second, the cleansing fountain of Zec 13:1 (VCG-05) — "a fountain opened... to cleanse them from sin and uncleanness" — has a christological-typological dimension: the fountain that will address the corporate/covenantal defilement at a future eschatological moment is widely understood in the tradition as pointing toward the atonement. Within §3 alone, Zec 13:1 carries its own eschatological-promissory typological weight without requiring external cross-reference.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. The pattern of unclean spirit possession, divine authority expelling the spirit, and the person restored — this narrative arc functions typologically for the NT's presentation of the kingdom of God. Mat 10:1 (VCG-03): authority over unclean spirits is paired with healing, framing it as a sign of the kingdom's arrival. Mar 3:11 (VCG-03) — the spirits' confession "You are the Son of God" — functions typologically as the cosmic acknowledgment of Christ's identity. The expulsion narratives function as enacted parables of the kingdom's defeat of the adversarial powers that hold humanity captive.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All four characteristics are E on typological use. The forms of typology differ significantly. Characteristic 1 carries two instances: the red-heifer purification rite (Num 19 — the most severe defilement/most elaborate remedy) pointing toward its divine antitype in Christ's cleansing (Heb 9:13-14 cross-reference, though outside the M10c corpus), and the Act 10:14/28 categorical revision showing the ritual-defilement boundary being dissolved as the eschatological signal of new-covenant extension to the nations. Characteristic 2 carries OT-to-NT typological scaffolding: the Hebrew prophetic inner-defilement voices (Job 14:4, Isa 6:5, Isa 64:6) name the problem that the NT claims is addressed in Christ; and the Rev 14:4 positive-inverse (undefiled following the Lamb as firstfruits) constitutes christological-eschatological typological participation. Characteristic 3 carries the land/sanctuary/name defilement-and-restoration arc as a type-antitype structure (physical defilement → eschatological cleansing: Eze 37:23, Isa 52:1, Zec 13:1), with the Zec 13:1 cleansing fountain carrying christological-promissory weight. Characteristic 4 carries the possession-expulsion-restoration narrative arc as enacted kingdom typology: each expulsion is a present anticipation of the eschatological defeat of all adversarial spiritual powers. The cluster thus shows the M10c domain as typologically pervasive — every register of defilement participates in a larger redemptive-eschatological economy.

questions.section: T0 — Divine Image and Created Design
questions.question_text: If typological use is present, what is the direction of the typology — does the human instance point toward the divine, or does the divine instance establish the pattern for the human?
questions.review_note: folded_into=T0.4.1 · tier-catalogue v2_1 refit 2026-06-19 · typological direction folded into the typology question

findings.session_b_note:
The direction is clear from the data and runs **divine-to-human** in its primary movement:

- The divine instance (God's forgiveness-character, God's act) establishes the pattern, the standard, and the ground for the human act.
- F-003 establishes the structural logic: "vertical reception (forgiveness from God) → inner transformation → horizontal extension (forgiveness extended to others)." The human act of forgiving flows from and is shaped by the received divine act.
- The parable of Mat 18:35 makes this explicit: the servant *who has received* forgiveness is expected to extend it. The divine-to-human direction is causal and normative.
- The one clear human-to-divine direction in the data is the intercession corpus (group 5379-002): the human person seeks forgiveness from God in prayer. But this is not typological — it is the access-posture, not a typological pointer.

*Adds structure:* The typology consistently runs from divine pattern to human imaging. The human act of forgiving does not point *toward* the divine but *derives from* the divine. This distinguishes forgiveness typologically from characteristics where the human instance may prefigure the divine.

findings.session_b_note:
The data reveals that the typological direction runs primarily from divine to human — but with a distinctive structural complication.

**Primary direction: divine to human.** The Exod 34:6 formula is the originating divine self-declaration that establishes the pattern. Joel 2:13 makes the direction explicit: God's compassion-character is cited as the reason the human is to "rend your hearts and return." The divine instance establishes the norm; human compassion is the responsive pattern. Similarly, the splanchnizō pattern in the Gospels shows Jesus's compassion establishing the pattern that is then named as the shape of neighbour-love (Luke 10:33 — "go and do likewise," v.37).

**Structural complication: the vocabulary runs upward.** As noted at T0.3 Prompt 1, the RACHAM root moves from the anatomical human (re.chem, womb) to the divine attribute (ra.cham, compassion). This means that at the level of vocabulary origin, the human bodily experience is the ground from which the divine character is named. The typological direction of the text (divine → human) and the etymological direction of the vocabulary (human body → divine attribute) run in opposite directions.

This is not a contradiction — it is analytically significant. The divine character of compassion is named through the human body precisely because that body is made in the image of God. The womb-language points back to the source from which it was drawn: what the human person experiences as the most intimate bodily care is what God is in his essential inner character. The typology is therefore bidirectional at a deep level, even if the normative movement of the text runs divine-to-human.

Similarly, the splanchnizō pattern in the Gospels shows Jesus's compassion establishing the pattern that is then named as the shape of neighbour-love (Luke 10:33 — "go and do likewise," v.37).

**Structural complication: the vocabulary runs upward.** As noted at T0.3 Prompt 1, the RACHAM root moves from the anatomical human (re.chem, womb) to the divine attribute (ra.cham, compassion). This means that at the level of vocabulary origin, the human bodily experience is the ground from which the divine character is named. The typological direction of the text (divine → human) and the etymological direction of the vocabulary (human body → divine attribute) run in opposite directions.

This is not a contradiction — it is analytically significant. The divine character of compassion is named through the human body precisely because that body is made in the image of God. The womb-language points back to the source from which it was drawn: what the human person experiences as the most intimate bodily care is what God is in his essential inner character. The typology is therefore bidirectional at a deep level, even if the normative movement of the text runs divine-to-human.

findings.session_b_note:
The direction is **human-to-divine**: the human experience of being crushed, broken, and made contrite before God provides the vocabulary and conceptual framework through which the Servant's unique substitutionary crushing is described. The human instance is the lexical and experiential source; the Servant-instance is the fulfilment and reversal.

The reversal is analytically significant: in the human penitential instances, the crushed person is the one who has sinned (Psa 51 — David post-Bathsheba) or the one who suffers under enmity or divine chastisement (Psa 143, Psa 44). In Isa 53:5, the crushed Servant has not sinned but is crushed for the iniquities of others. The direction of guilt is inverted — the crushing falls where it does not belong, producing outcomes (peace, healing) for those who bear the guilt. The typological direction: human contrition (the sinner crushed by their moral condition) → Servant's vicarious crushing (the innocent crushed for sinners) → outcomes of peace and healing for the community.

*New finding: the typological inversion — innocent crushed for the guilty, reversing the expected penitential direction — has not been named explicitly in prior analysis. This is an analytically significant assembly of existing data (OBS-030-026, OBS-030-041, OBS-030-042).*

findings.session_b_note:
The direction is bidirectional and varies by group.

**Divine-to-human direction:** In 2Pe 1:4, the divine nature is the *telos* toward which human participation moves. God's nature establishes the pattern; human fellowship points toward it. The direction is: divine origin → human participation → divine fullness. God's nature is the destination.

**Human-to-divine direction (via Christ):** In Phili 3:10, Paul's fellowship with Christ's sufferings participates in the christological pattern (death-resurrection). The human instance (Paul's suffering) points toward and participates in the divine pattern (Christ's resurrection). The direction is: human suffering → fellowship with Christ's death → resurrection. Here the human instance *points toward* the divine reality by participating in it.

**Covenantal-to-eschatological direction:** In Eze 37:19, the physical joining of the sticks points toward national restoration, which itself points toward the eschatological community. The human/national instance points toward the divine fulfilment.

**New finding:** Fellowship is not typologically unidirectional. Its typological structure is participatory — the human enters the divine pattern, and in entering it, is oriented toward its fullness. This is distinct from the simpler form of typology where a human event merely foreshadows a divine one without genuine participation.

findings.session_b_note: The direction is consistently divine-to-human. Mic 6:8 makes this explicit: "He has told you, O man, what is good" — the definition of goodness flows from God to the human person. Gen 1:31 establishes goodness as a divine creative-evaluative reality before any human instance exists. Psa 119:68 ("You are good... teach me") confirms the direction: human goodness is learned from and patterned on divine goodness. The divine instance is originating and pattern-setting; the human instance is derived, responsive, and participatory. There is no movement in the data where human goodness is the type pointing to a divine antitype. (OBS-067-OBS-001, OBS-067-OBS-026)

findings.session_b_note: The evidence shows both directions operating but with a clear asymmetry. In the OT prophetic tradition: human marital/parental love → divine covenantal love (the human type points toward and is fulfilled in the divine). In the NT: divine love → human love (the divine instance establishes the pattern for the human: 'as I have loved you' — Joh 13:34; 'we love because he first loved us' — 1Jo 4:19). The asymmetry is that in the NT the direction inverts: the human type has served its purpose; the divine original now directly constitutes the human instance. The love-structure of the inner being therefore participates in a typological movement across the canon: created human love → figures divine love → divine love in Christ becomes the source and standard of human love in the new covenant.

findings.session_b_note: The evidence shows both directions, operating differently in the covenant vocabulary. The primary direction is divine → human → divine: God establishes the covenantal pattern (Noahic, Abrahamic, Mosaic, Davidic), the human community receives and participates in it, and those OT covenants point typologically forward to the new covenant enacted by Christ (divine initiative completing what the prior covenants anticipated). The Gal 4:24 allegorical reading (OBS-034-071) has God establishing the divine archetype (Sarah/new Jerusalem) which judges and supersedes the human instance (Hagar/Sinai). The secondary direction is human → divine: the human marriage covenant (H1285 1a5, H3748 divorce — OBS-034-012, OBS-034-043) is used as the vehicle for understanding the God-Israel relationship — the human instance illuminates the divine by analogy. This is the metaphorical direction. Both directions are active; the primary typological movement is from OT covenant realities pointing forward to the new covenant in Christ.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — and structurally so. The OT vocabulary names peace as a condition to be given, a covenant to be kept, a king to come. The NT vocabulary names peace as a person present: G1515 group 426-003 (Eph 2:14 — "he himself is our peace," OBS-117-122 from prior session). The Greek eirēnē carries all the semantic range of shalom (established by the LXX translation pattern) and then names Christ as the one in whom all those dimensions converge. The NT fullness: (1) Peace with God (Rom 5:1) — the relational condition; (2) Peace of God guarding hearts and minds (Phili 4:7) — the inner condition; (3) Christ IS peace (Eph 2:14) — the person; (4) Spirit-fruit peace (Gal 5:22) — the gift; (5) cosmic peace-making through the blood of the cross (Col 1:20, G1517 group 430-001) — the mechanism. The OT's four shalom dimensions (felt state, relational condition, divine gift, eschatological reality) are not rejected in the NT but fulfilled in a single person.

findings.session_b_note: The direction is primarily divine-to-human: the divine instance establishes the pattern that the human instance echoes and participates in. The primary direction across all seven sub-groups is divine-to-human: the divine instance establishes the pattern and standard; the human instance is the derivative participation. The one exception is M05-F where the mother-comfort (Isa 66:13 — Group 1742) runs human-to-divine — a rare upward-pointing typology from human experience to divine reality. In M05-E, the Zec 9:9 typology (human kingly meekness pointing toward the messianic king) also has an upward dimension. But the dominant direction is: divine establishes → human participates.
**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Divine-to-human: God's righteousness establishes the pattern, and the Messianic types participate in and point toward the divine instance.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Human-to-divine: Abraham's human righteousness (credited by faith) points typologically toward a larger reality — all who believe participate in the same credited righteousness (Rom 4:23–24). The suffering righteous person of the Psalms (M26-A2-016) points toward Christ.
**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Divine-established-pattern toward Messianic expression — the divine uprightness establishes what the Messianic king's scepter represents.

**[C — Justification]** Human-to-divine: the human judicial pattern (acquit the innocent, Deu 25:1) points toward the divine judicial act of justification. God uses the human courtroom as a type and then surpasses the type by justifying the ungodly by faith.
**[D — Avenging Justice]** Human-to-divine: Moses' act points typologically toward Christ as the deliverer rejected by Israel.
**[E — Condemnation]** Human historical instance points toward eschatological divine judgment.
**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Human-instance-revealing-divine-pattern: Abraham's case reveals the divine pattern (credited righteousness), then divine pattern applied to all subsequent believers.

**[CLUSTER]** Both directions of typology are present in M26, but the dominant direction is human-to-divine: human instances of righteousness, justice, and reckoning point toward and are fulfilled by the divine instance in Christ. The exception is A1, where the divine establishes the pattern and the creaturely instances participate in it downward. This confirms the cluster's essential structure: A1 is the source from which all other sub-groups derive their meaning.

Consistently top-down: divine establishes the pattern; human instance participates. Christ as Wisdom (A) → human wisdom received. Christ opens minds (B) → understanding given. Divine word dwelling (H) → human constituted by it. The typological direction is always divine → human.

findings.finding_value: In M01-A, the direction is from human instance to eschatological/divine confirmation: human reverential fear now anticipates the fullness of that posture in the final state (Rev 14:7; 19:5). The Isa 11:2-3 messianic typology moves from the divine instance (the Spirit of the Lord resting on the king in fear-of-God) establishing the pattern for what perfect fear-of-God looks like in the human person.

In M01-B's christological encounters, the direction is from the human encounter (disciples' fear) outward to the divine reality being revealed: the fear functions as the experiential marker that what is present exceeds natural categories. The direction is from human response → revelation of divine identity.

In M01-C's conquest typology, the direction is from divine act (God's terror-weapon) → confirming divine ownership of history. The human instance (terror in Israel's enemies) points to the divine sovereignty established over all powers.

Gal 1:4 (vc=14466 — VCG-01) points from the present experience of the "evil age" toward the rescue that transcends it — the present age as type points to its transcendence. The VCG-01 cosmic-evil evidence (evil one, evil age) also introduces a typological direction from the cosmic domain downward to the personal: 1Jo 5:19 (vc=14433 — VCG-01 — "the whole world lies in the power of the evil one") frames the cosmic evil as the context that explains the constitutional human condition.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The typological direction runs from present human moral conditions toward eschatological divine verdict. The OT Proverbs and Prophets identify specific inner-being conditions as abominable (crooked heart, silenced conscience, dishonest practice) — these present human instances point toward the eschatological separation of Rev 21:27 (nothing abominable enters the holy city). The Revelation material takes the moral-character abomination category and deploys it at cosmic scale (Rev 17:5 — Babylon as mother of abominations), showing that present moral abomination patterns ultimately find their fullest expression and judgment in cosmic-eschatological terms. The typological movement is from the particular (this heart, this act) toward the universal (all abomination excluded from the divine presence). No typological use points from a divine instance downward to the human.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The typological direction runs from historical idolatrous abomination patterns (OT) toward eschatological and cosmic sacrilege events (Daniel's prophecy → NT apocalyptic). Dan 9:27 and Dan 11:31 (VCG-06 — historical desecration under Antiochus) are taken up in Mat 24:15 and Mar 13:14 (VCG-06) as pointing toward a future eschatological event. The typological movement is from the particular historical instances (Baal-peor — Hos 9:10; Manasseh's idolatry — 2Ki 21:2; Ezekiel's vision of the sanctuary — VCG-05) toward a culminating eschatological abomination-of-desolation event. The direction is from human instances of idolatrous abomination in the present, pointing forward and upward toward an eschatological-cosmic fulfillment of the pattern.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The typological direction runs from specific human instances of scheming iniquity toward the general theological assertion about divine justice. The particular instances (those who devise iniquitous decrees — Isa 10:1 — VCG-02; those who plot treachery — Psa 59:5 — vc=38242 — VCG-03; those who lay snares — Psa 141:9 — vc=38231 — VCG-03) function as instances of a pattern that points toward the universal divine verdict on all such scheming. The direction is from the human-particular upward to the divine-universal: each specific act of inner scheming participates in a type whose full meaning is the certainty of divine judgment on all iniquity. No typology runs from divine instance downward to human.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The typological direction is from present/historical instances toward eschatological culmination, and from human instances toward christological revelation. Rev 13:6 (VCG-01): the beast's blasphemy as the concentrated eschatological type of all human blasphemous defiance — present instances of cursing God (Rev 16:9/11/21 — VCG-01) participate in and anticipate this eschatological beast-blasphemy. Joh 18:30 (VCG-03): the false charge against the innocent man as evildoer — the human instance of false accusation is typologically loaded in the christological context; the one falsely charged as an evildoer is the one who is in fact the righteous one. The direction is: present human instances of evil speech → eschatological beast-type concentration of blasphemy (Rev 13:6); and historical false accusation → christological revelation of its wrongness (Joh 18:30).

**[CLUSTER]** E — Across all six characteristics, the typological direction is consistent: from present human instances outward to eschatological or cosmic reality, with no divine-instance-to-human typology in any characteristic. The direction is unanimously human-particular → universal-eschatological. No characteristic shows a divine instance of wickedness, evil, or abomination establishing a pattern for the human — this is structurally impossible given T0.1.2's unanimous denial of divine possession. The variation within this unanimous direction: Chars 1 and 5 show individual human instances → universal divine-justice verdict (the wicked schemer's fate typifying all such scheming's fate). Chars 3 and 4 show OT historical instances → eschatological cosmic events (historical abominations → abomination of desolation). Char 6 shows human false-accusation instances → christological revelation (Joh 18:30 → Christ's trial). Char 2 shows the present evil age as type → rescue transcending it (Gal 1:4). The cluster's typological direction is consistently ascending (human → cosmic/eschatological) rather than descending (divine → human) — confirming that the M10b cluster addresses failure-conditions of the creaturely sphere that point toward the eschatological resolution of those failures.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The direction is bidirectional within the two typological instances identified at T0.4.1. In the Num 19 red-heifer rite, the human ritual instance (the most severe defilement state and its prescribed remedy) points forward and upward toward its divine antitype — the rite is the shadow; the cleansing power of Christ's sacrifice is the substance. In the Act 10 categorical revision, the divine initiative (God's voice declaring what is clean) establishes the pattern: the old human category (unclean persons/nations) is dissolved by divine speech, showing the divine instance as authoritative over the ritual category. In both cases, the ritual-defilement-state is the human creaturely structure that the divine economy uses as its scaffolding.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The direction is from the human negative instance toward the divine-eschatological positive. The Hebrew moral-inner defilement descriptions (Job 14:4, Isa 6:5, Isa 64:6, VCG-01) name a human problem in need of divine resolution — they point forward to the NT announcement that the problem is addressed. The call at 1Th 4:7 (VCG-02) — "God has not called us for impurity, but in holiness" — frames the divine calling as the telos that the person is moving toward. The typological direction is: human defilement (present) → divine call to holiness (active) → eschatological fullness of holiness (Rev 14:4) — human-to-eschatological. The divine does not establish defilement as a pattern for the human; the divine call to holiness establishes the goal the human defilement-state must be left behind.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The direction runs from the historical-covenantal instance toward the eschatological-divine antitype. The defilement of land, sanctuary, and name through Israel's corporate moral defection (the present historical instance evidenced in the pre-exilic corpus) points forward to a future divine act of comprehensive cleansing that exceeds the ritual and political restorations of the OT period. Eze 37:23 (VCG-05): "I will save... and will cleanse them" — the divine subject of the future cleansing is God himself; the human corporate defilement (the type) requires divine action (the antitype). The typological direction is thus upward and forward: from creaturely corporate failure toward divine eschatological redemption.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The direction is from the present historical instance toward the eschatological-divine antitype. The individual possession-and-expulsion events in the gospel narratives (Mar 1:23-27, Mar 5:2-13, Luk 8:29, Luk 9:42, VCG-01 and -02) are particular instances pointing forward to the comprehensive eschatological defeat of all adversarial spiritual powers. The divine instance — Christ's authority over unclean spirits — establishes the pattern: divine authority is supreme, and their defeat in individual cases anticipates their ultimate defeat at the consummation.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four characteristics show two typological directions, which themselves reveal a cluster-level pattern. Characteristic 1 shows a bidirectional typology: the Num 19 red-heifer rite (human creaturely structure pointing forward to divine antitype) and the Act 10 categorical revision (divine voice establishing the pattern by dissolving the human category). Characteristics 2, 3, and 4 all show the same direction: from the human historical instance upward and forward toward the divine-eschatological antitype. In all three cases the human defilement-state is the problem (the type) and divine action is the resolution (the antitype) — human moral-inner defilement resolved by the divine call to holiness and eschatological completion (Char 2); human corporate defilement resolved by divine eschatological cleansing (Char 3); human spirit-invasion resolved by divine authority and kingdom arrival (Char 4). The cluster-level pattern: Characteristic 1's typology is the most internally complex (bidirectional); Characteristics 2, 3, and 4 share the same direction (human problem → divine resolution), confirming the cluster's fundamental theological grammar: defilement is the creaturely problem; divine holiness, authority, and cleansing are the divine resolution.

findings.session_b_note: The fulfilment of peace in Christ reveals that the original design was for the human person to live in the peace of God — not a condition achieved by the person but a Person known. The "YHWH-Shalom" altar name (406-001) names God as peace in the context of a theophany — the human person encountering God, receiving peace, and naming God as its source and substance. The fulfilment in Christ (Eph 2:14 — he himself is our peace) reveals that this was always the design: peace is not an abstract inner state but a relational reality grounded in the presence of the one who IS peace. The original design for the human person was to dwell in God's peace through covenant fellowship — and the NT peace in Christ is the restoration and fulfilment of that original design. The "dividing wall of hostility" broken down (Eph 2:14) is not a new problem solved but an original rupture healed.
